text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
---Danish Insurance company Danica went into profit on its accident insurance business in 1996, earning 92 million crowns after a loss of 45 million the year before.

---At a cost of around one billion crowns, BG Bank is buying itself out of the SDC data alliance with smaller banks, leaving itself free to make new partnerships as it sees fit, without the smaller banks' approval.

---Danish exports to eastern Europe, notably Poland, Russia and the Baltic states, are doing so well that the former communist states will shortly qualify to be listed in Denmark's top 10 overseas markets ahead of European Union countries like Spain & Belgium. Danish exports to Poland shot 30 percent up last year. The Danish products enjoying most export success are machinery, food, chemicals and consumer goods.

--Danish telecommunications group Tele Danmark persists in its refusal to refund thousands of telephone subscribers excess charges paid since 1990, despite criticism from the state telecommunications board. Tele Danmark claims it made no profits during a transitional period when local phone call rates underwent changes to fit in with municipal boundaries and denies that the board has any longer the right to set charges.

--Danish economists cautiously expect that Denmark will still have a current account surplus in 1997, although they say much depends on the growth rate in its chief export market Germany. A 1996 surplus of 10.9 billion crowns was announced by the statistics office.

---The recent years' low inflation rates in Denmark have been a boon to old age pensioners who get more out of their pensions than expected. For society as a whole overall pension funds were worth 12 billion Dkk more in 1995 than foreseen in 1990 and the trend continued last year.
